title: What If a Supernova Exploded 26 Light-Years Away?
subject: supernova

scenes.text: What if a star exploded near us? At this distance, the danger isn't light. It's the sky itself.
NASA scientists calculated that a supernova within about 26 light-years could wreck Earth's ozone layer.
Gamma rays would split nitrogen in the air. The new chemicals could destroy roughly 47 percent of the ozone.
Ultraviolet light at the surface would roughly double, and the gamma ray exposure would last 300 to 500 days.
Cosmic rays could keep hitting for at least ten years, long enough to do lasting harm to life.
The good news: a blast that close happens about once every 670 million years. Earth just waits.
